downstream_requirements.title: Feedback anchoring over visual content, and feedback delivery back to the originating task
downstream_requirements.status: recorded as a requirement and a qualification case. Not implemented, not designed, not in scope for this turn.

what_exists: Block anchors: FeedbackNote carries block_id and block_label — crates/codeflow-present/src/state.rs:166-174.

Exact text-selection anchors: FeedbackNote.selector is an optional TextSelector of start_utf16/end_utf16, and FeedbackAnchor resolves to Block, Anchored, Reanchored or Orphaned with quote-and-context re-anchoring — crates/codeflow-present/src/state.rs:157-219, re-anchor logic at 2238-2290.
what_does_not_exist: Any coordinate, region, shape or element anchor over an image, a diagram or a rendered figure. FeedbackAnchor has exactly four variants and all four are block- or text-offset based. A reader cannot point at a mark in a figure; they can only point at the block that contains it.

Any automatic delivery of feedback into the originating Codex or Claude task. `codeflow present feedback --follow` writes newline-delimited JSON envelopes to stdout and marks them delivered in the store — crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/present.rs:557-574. Nothing carries an envelope into a harness conversation.
confirmed_gap.the_naming_hazard: FeedbackLifecycle::Delivered (state.rs:203-209) is set by mark_delivered when an envelope is written to stdout. That is storage and transport state. It is not evidence that any harness, agent or human received the feedback, and it must never be reported as chat delivery.

constraints_on_any_eventual_direction: Anchoring must survive a revision. Whatever a visual anchor points at needs the equivalent of the existing quote-and-context re-anchor: a stable visual-element or region identity, with an explicit orphaned state when the figure changes underneath it, not a raw pixel coordinate that silently drifts.

The feedback envelope stays harness-neutral. Delivery is an adapter behind it, each adapter separately qualified, each with a declared fallback, and the fallback is what happens when no adapter is present — not a silent success.
Storage is never reported as delivery. A lifecycle that cannot distinguish 'written to stdout' from 'received by the task' is the defect, not the transport.
downstream_requirements.why_it_is_here_and_not_in_production: The visual and content direction is unsettled and operator-owned. An anchor model that points at visual elements is a consequence of how figures are composed and what identity a mark carries — which is exactly what this board is trying to settle. Building a host adapter first would fix the anchor model to whatever the first adapter happened to need.
downstream_requirements.qualification_case: Once a direction is selected, the selected composition must be able to name its own information-bearing marks stably enough to anchor to, and the board's own figures are the fixture for testing that. A direction that cannot give a mark a durable identity cannot support visual feedback, and that is a scoring input, not an afterthought.
downstream_requirements.scope_boundary_for_this_turn: No runtime, schema, portal or CLI change was made for R1. Only this record.
